chose: Scope's HTTP token and port persist per root in .coherence/run/http.json (mode 0600): a random 32-byte token made by the first server, and the port it was assigned, asked for again after a restart
over: a fresh token and OS-assigned port per server process
because: the owner wants the page to update as it goes and to show disconnected then reconnect; a page cannot learn a new token or port, so a per-process secret would strand every open page at each restart or code-fingerprint replacement. Deleting http.json rotates the token

chose: The live page reads Server-Sent Events through fetch with the token in an Authorization header; the token appears in an address only for the shell document the launcher opens, and the API refuses it in a query
over: EventSource with the token in the stream's address; a cookie
because: EventSource cannot send headers, and a token in every request address ends up in more places; a header a cross-origin page cannot make the browser add is the stronger defense, and a cookie would be sent by the browser on any page's request to the port

chose: A reconnecting page sends cursors derived from its state; the server's catch-up reaches 60 s before each cursor and the page merges by key (journal id, run time and session, work id)
over: a strict after-cursor catch-up as journal --since does; server-side sequence numbers
because: two writers can append out of time order, so a record stamped before the page's latest can land after it and a strict cursor would lose it; a keyed merge makes the overlap harmless, and sequence numbers would not survive a server restart

chose: The warm server starts HTTP only when asked (the http socket method from coherence scope), or at start on a root whose http.json records a port; status, stop and http are answered outside the instrument queue
over: HTTP always on in every hook-spawned server; every method in the queue
because: a hook-spawned server in every worktree should not bind a port nobody reads, but a root whose reading was opened should answer an open page after a restart; and a quick question queued behind a cold project load would trip its short client timeout on a healthy server
